_readme: Copy this file to local.settings.json and fill in the values. local.settings.json is excluded from git.

Values._SmartTableSync:Mode_readme: Manual (default): scaffold the child DB by hand via SmartTableSync.Scaffold, then add tables to TableList once applied. Auto: the Function creates/updates child DDL itself on first sight of a table or parent schema drift - requires ChildProvisioningConnectionString below.
Values._ChildProvisioningConnectionString_readm: Only required when SmartTableSync:Mode is Auto. Uses the smarttablesync-child-provisioning identity (see sql/07_permissions.sql) - the same one SmartTableSync.Scaffold already uses, never the runtime identity above.
Values._SmartTableSync:TimestampColumns_readme: Per-table datetime column the Timestamp strategy filters on. A table not listed here defaults to 'LastUpdate'. Example: "SmartTableSync:TimestampColumns:SomeOtherTable": "ModifiedAt". The original key name, SmartTableSync:ChangeTrackingColumns:<Table>, is still read; the new name wins if both are set.
Values._SmartTableSync:AllowFullRescanFor_readm: Comma-separated table names explicitly allowed to fall back to a full-table re-scan every run when no other strategy applies, even above 50,000 rows. Smaller tables fall back automatically without being listed here.
Values._SmartTableSync:IncrementalStrategyOverr: Per-table override of the auto-derived incremental strategy (Timestamp/FullRescan/RowVersion/SqlChangeTracking). Without this, a table with SQL Server Change Tracking enabled uses SqlChangeTracking, and a detected rowversion column wins over a configured/default datetime column. The override is validated against the table's actual schema at provisioning time - e.g. forcing RowVersion on a table with no rowversion column throws. Example: "SmartTableSync:IncrementalStrategyOverrides:SomeTable": "Timestamp".
Values._SmartTableSync:KeyColumns_readme: Per-table key columns, comma-separated in key order, for a table with no PRIMARY KEY and no unique index whose key columns are all NOT NULL. The columns must be NOT NULL and unique together; duplicates are checked against the parent's data when the table is set up. The child table gets them as its PRIMARY KEY. Change Tracking still needs a real PRIMARY KEY. Example: "SmartTableSync:KeyColumns:sales.Ledger": "Region,Code".
Values._SmartTableSync:ReconcileIntervalHours_r: How often (whole hours, default 1) tables on every strategy except SqlChangeTracking compare parent and child keys to remove deleted rows - their only source of deletes, so 0 is not allowed.
Values._SmartTableSync:ChangeTrackingReconcileI: Same safety net for SqlChangeTracking tables, which already receive deletes every cycle (default 24; 0 = only after a fallback full re-scan).
Values._SmartTableSync:ConnectionOpenAttempts_r: Total attempts (1-60, default 5) to open a database connection on a transient error such as an Azure SQL failover or throttling, with exponential backoff. 1 disables retries.
